>>253750977
I think there is a better than 50/50 chance either a vaccine will not be found, or it will take 10 years. SARS 1.0 doesn't have a vaccine, and not from lack of trying. If one is found there is a real possibility of it not being very safe and/or requiring annual or semiannual boosters. In the meantime it's going to be a heavy health burden on par with a modern TB. 

> If it were not for mass rapid transportation and population density--caused by modern tech--then the virus would have been geographically isolated. 
The nearest horseshoe bat populations to Wuhan are hundreds of miles south so either someone went cave spelunking to harvest bats as a novelty item for rich urbanites to each, or it escaped the lab. Somehow I doubt bats are a staple food item for any primitive cultures, I can't imagine a bat has many calories.
